He came in the evening, and I'm almost certain that for reasons of his own he went to Belgrade in the morning. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Did you have contact with him when he returned to the Leva Supoderica command post?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Late in the evening when he asked for the numbers of men. It was already winter so it had been dark for a long time already. It was in the evening. I couldn't tell you what time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question of military nature. I saw in your military record that in 1992 you were promoted lieutenant, so I'm sure you will immediately understand my question. When Mr. Kameni leaves for Belgrade during the day, obviously, who takes command in his absence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in question? Is it you? Are you the one in command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was a platoon commander. If Kameni went somewhere, he probably appointed someone to be acting commander. On such occasions, it could have been Katic if he wasn't with him, Kinez, Ceca. He could simply appoint someone for the period of time of his absence to be acting commander,, not to command but to be a sort of duty officer in the command, to keep an eye on things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your unit was there a duty officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mrs. Dahl, we have about five minutes before the end of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: When Kameni came back from Belgrade, what was his state of mind or his physical presence when he contacted you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: When he came back from Belgrade I did not see him, that very moment when he returned from Belgrade. Quite simply, I didn't need him, I had no questions for him, and nothing was happening at the front. I saw him later when he called all platoon commanders via courier to come to a meeting, when he told us to check personnel levels, that people should not be allowed to stroll about. When people are idle and just strolling about, they are prone to looting. So that is how I understood his orders. That's when I saw him. Now, whether he was upset or not, well, he was quite upset, tired. I don't know how to describe this to you now. Quite simply, he was tired.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Can you describe his demeanour? Was he -- I don't want to put words in your mouth. I'm interested in what you observed from him.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: As commander, he was always a cool, calm man; otherwise, he would not have been a commander. He's a reasonable man, but of course he would get tired, upset, and any incident could upset him. He's a human being too, quite simply. Then, like all the rest of us, he was already tired and upset enough. But at that moment I didn't know why he was upset and I did not investigate that, and to tell you quite frankly, I didn't care. I was there, I carried out my order, and that's the kind of relationship we had. We never disrupted that relationship. I always knew that I was the subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Did his demeanour cause you to think that there was something wrong or something out of the ordinary?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, after the personnel were counted, one realized that something was not right. He did not mention the TO or Miroljub, but quite simply the man did not want to make everything public straight away. He didn't want to disturb the soldiers too, probably, but he just told us probably what he thought was sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think we should end now. It's almost 1.15. Sir, you are under oath. You're a witness of justice now and you cannot contact the Prosecution. We will meet tomorrow morning and -- at 8.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I would ask for a complete instruction. It would be inappropriate for him to contact either the Prosecution or the Defence or to discuss his testimony with anyone else, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, obviously. That's obvious, it goes without saying. But, Witness, you can contact no one, absolutely no one. Thank you. The hearing is adjourned and we will meet tomorrow at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of January, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.
